items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The director of "Chez florence" was Madame Regina

ctx.x: But I enjoyed working at "Chez Florence" in Willie's orchestra. We started work at 11 p.m. and played until 1 a.m. and then had one-and-half hours off. A French orchestra played during our off time and when we came back, we worked until 5 or 6 o'clock in the morning, depending on how many people that stayed until that time. The good thing about working at "Chez Florence" was that there were no afternoon tea dancing there.

The director of "Chez florence" was Madame Regina and the Maitre d'hotel(head waiter) and second director was a Monsieur Victor. Another good thing about working there was that I did not have to take a bus or taxi to work as it was 12 minutes walking distance from where I lived and 2 minutes to Boudon's cafe.

At the "Chez florence" there was never actually what you would call a show. There were entertainers, and they would have a singer. Apart from that we played dance music - a lot of it was just commercial orchestrations. Often, when I'd take my solo, I'd have to blow into my stand to keep it from being too loud. I always like to blow out, because it's difficult to play with the same intensity quietly. If you feel free to blow, it's easier to get the feeling.
